notes: Lamport logical clocks maintain causal event ordering using happens-before relations across message passing.
Physical clock drift and offsets are simulated mathematically because all nodes execute on a single physical host.
All Berkeley round polling, replies, and clock adjustments use real UDP datagrams on loopback socket bindings.
UDP transport is connectionless and unacknowledged: messages transmitted to crashed nodes report delivery status UNKNOWN.

The time daemon is the leader elected by Experiment 4. With no leader yet, the first Berkeley round asks Experiment 4 for an election, which starts its election service and heartbeats on every live node; if no leader can be elected, the round is refused.
